title: El Tiny 2026 Lineup: Los Tigres del Norte, Mon Laferte, and More Behind the Desk
summary: Every year, NPR's famous Tiny Desk concert series gets a new name and a new vibe. For Hispanic Heritage Month, it becomes El Tiny — a month-long celebration of Latin American and Latino artists. The 2026 lineup was just announced, and it's stacked with talent from across the Spanish-speaking world. From September 15 through October 15, artists like Los Tigres del Norte, Mon Laferte, Draco Rosa, Yendry, and many more will perform behind the desk. "Since 2021, NPR's El Tiny concert series has brought the best of Latin music to new audiences, reminding us of music's remarkable ability to connect us across borders, generations and cultures," said Felix Contreras, co-host of Alt.Latino and co-producer of El Tiny. "This year's lineup continues to reaffirm that Latin music is the world's music and is something worth celebrating." Anamaria Sayre, co-host of Alt.Latino and co-producer of El Tiny, added, "Both Tiny Desk and Alt.Latino have always been about bringing people closer to the artists and music that move us. El Tiny is a celebration of that spirit and of the incredible breadth, creativity and history of Latin music." The Tiny Desk series has a strong history with Latin artists. Bad Bunny, Karol G, and Grupo Frontera have all delivered memorable performances. One standout: Ca7riel and Paco Amoroso's 2024 set has 55 million views on YouTube. This year's full lineup includes Mon Laferte, Los Mirlos, Yendry, Alex Ferreira, Melissa Aldana and Gonzalo Rubalcaba, Panteón Rocóco, Tim Bernardes, Los Texmaniacs, Draco Rosa, and Los Tigres del Norte. Dates are still to be announced. Sayre said, "Whether you're a devoted fan or discovering these artists for the first time, there's something special about hearing them on the intimate Tiny Desk stage and we hope you find some new favorites in our lineup."
why_it_matters: El Tiny shows that cultural influence is not only about charts and stadium tours: a public broadcaster's tiny stage can introduce millions of listeners to artists from across Latin America, and heritage months have become a mainstream way for media to reflect a country's changing population.

background_read: Tiny Desk Concerts began at NPR (National Public Radio, the United States' non-profit public radio network) when a host squeezed a band behind his office desk, and the format has since become one of the most-watched live-music series online. El Tiny is its Spanish-language sibling, launched in 2021 — the same year the show Alt.Latino (NPR's long-running Latin music program) began co-producing it.

Hispanic Heritage Month runs from September 15 to October 15 in the United States. The mid-September start marks the independence days of several Central American countries, with Mexico's following on September 16 and Chile's on September 18 — which is why the celebration spans two calendar months.

The 2026 lineup stretches across generations and styles: Los Tigres del Norte (a Mexican norteño band that has sold millions of records and told story-songs about migrant life since the 1970s), Mon Laferte (a Chilean singer-songwriter known for mixing bolero, rock, and pop), and Draco Rosa (a Puerto Rican artist and former member of the boy band Menudo).

Earlier Tiny Desk and El Tiny sets by Bad Bunny (a Puerto Rican global pop star), Karol G (a Colombian reggaeton singer), and Grupo Frontera drew huge audiences — proof that a small office desk can now compete with major streaming events for Latin music fans.

perspectives.perspective: Positive — wider exposure for Latin music
perspectives.description: Putting artists like Los Tigres del Norte and Mon Laferte behind a famous desk gives them a new global audience, and the intimacy of Tiny Desk lets listeners hear musicians in a way big concerts rarely allow. For fans, it is also a bridge between generations and genres, from norteño to bolero to reggaeton.

perspectives.perspective: Critical — a month is not a year
perspectives.description: Some argue that celebrating Latin music in one dedicated month can look like tokenism when English-language acts dominate the rest of the schedule. Others note that lumping very different national traditions under one label such as 'the world's music' can flatten the differences the series says it celebrates.

perspectives.perspective: Neutral / analytical — a familiar media pattern
perspectives.description: Public broadcasters in many countries have long used heritage months to build relationships with audiences they had previously underserved, and those efforts usually follow demographic change rather than lead it. In that sense El Tiny is part of a broader shift in how U.S. media programmes for Spanish-speaking listeners.

perspectives.perspective: Forward-looking — from a month to year-round
perspectives.description: The real measure of success will be whether these artists keep appearing on Tiny Desk and Alt.Latino outside September and October, and whether the series keeps investing in Latin music beyond the spotlight month. If listeners stick around, a temporary label like El Tiny could permanently change who the show features.
